# Additions to Esther Chapter 6 (Addition F) — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther F | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_006_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition F: Mordecai looks back at his dream and now sees what it meant all along. The book ends with its translator's note.]*

**1** Then Mordecai said: "All of this has come from God.

**2** I remember the dream I had about all of this. And not one thing in it has failed to come true.

**3** The little spring that turned into a great river — the light and the sun and the rushing water — that was Esther. The king married her and made her his queen.

**4** The two dragons? That was Haman. And that was me.

**5** The nations who gathered to destroy — they were the ones who came against the name of the Jews.

**6** And my own people — that is Israel, the ones who cried out to God and were rescued. The Lord saved his people. The Lord pulled us out of all these disasters. And God performed great signs and wonders, the like of which have never been seen among the nations.

**7** For this — all of this — he had prepared two lots: one for the people of God, and one for all the other nations.

**8** And those two lots came into play at the appointed time, on the day of reckoning, before God and before all the nations.

**9** And God remembered his people. He vindicated his inheritance.

**10** So they will celebrate these days in the month of Adar — the fourteenth and fifteenth — with gathering together and joy and gladness before God. Every generation. Forever. Among his people Israel."

**11** [Translator's colophon:] In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemy and Cleopatra, a man named Dositheus — who claimed to be a priest and a Levite — and his son Ptolemy, brought this letter about Purim. They said it had been translated by Lysimachus son of Ptolemy, someone who lived in Jerusalem.
